comparison.interpretation: Once complete-store absence was proven, explicitly compiling empty-set identities fixed the one count and two existence questions. It did not materially increase accepted tokens.

excluded_zero_call_attempts.reason: The model-visible packet guard rejected the nested key named answer before any model call. The receipt schema was renamed to empty_value.
The harness rejected the 409-row input versus 23-row packet mismatch before any model call. The successful arm pinned all 23 question IDs.

scoring.answer_equivalence: Scalar [] accepts a no-matching-result response; count [[0]] requires 0; boolean [[0]] requires no/false.
scoring.mechanism_rule: The response must attribute the empty dependent event set to the proven absence of a current/open hospital Encounter.

anti_leakage.important_boundary: The empty-scope operator is a narrow question-text heuristic built on burned development wording. It is a context-compiler control, not an independently validated planner.

claims_supported: For these 23 burned questions, a terminal complete-store Encounter search can prove that the current hospital-Encounter set is empty.
A model often converts that proof into empty scalar answers, but it needs explicit result algebra to reliably distinguish no matching scalar, count zero, and existence false.
The result does not require a native graph database; it used ordinary FHIR search plus a typed compiler receipt.
claims_not_supported: Graph traversal generally improves clinical question answering.
The result generalizes beyond these three patients, these 23 burned questions, this model episode, or snapshot-open benchmark semantics.
The store-complete arm can retrieve positive current-visit events; every case in this slice had an empty current-Encounter scope.
The question-text operator classifier is production-ready.
next_experiment: Build complete inverse Encounter-to-event retrieval on positive and missing-root burned cases, emit per-resource-family terminal-pagination receipts, and compare strict family selection with a declared cross-resource fallback.
